notes.cutoff: Data cut-off: the latest EGX close is Wednesday 25 November (EGX30 50,538.66); Thursday's session has not opened. Brent and gold are Thursday-morning Asian-trading prices; Wall Street is Wednesday's close and US markets are shut on Thursday. The CBE's dollar rate is EnterpriseAM's Thursday market table. Gold prices in EGP are Banky's Thursday prices. Bullish and bearish tags are directional reads of the news, not trade recommendations.
notes.unverified: Not verified and therefore left out: Wednesday's net flows by nationality, because Amwal Al Ghad reports Egyptians as net buyers of EGP 4.65 bn and foreigners as net sellers of EGP 4.73 bn, while EnterpriseAM reports local investors as the only net sellers; Brent's Wednesday settlement, because Investing.com gives $90.91 (February contract) while Reuters' Thursday figures imply a close near $94.6 (the chart is flagged); the US crude stock forecast (1.5 mn or 2 mn barrels); Thursday's Asian index moves, which differ within the same Investing.com page; the Suez Canal's net tonnage growth rate, because Amwal Al Ghad's 92.2% does not match its own 72 mn and 37 mn ton figures; Wednesday's advancing and declining stocks. Egypt Aluminum's rows before 18 November no longer appear in the six sessions shown.
notes.sourcesFoot: All 21 StockAnalysis pages opened on Thursday morning and show Wednesday 25 November as the latest session.

items: The Saudi-led coalition strikes Yemen's Hodeidah port, and the Houthis threaten all Saudi Red Sea ports, including Jeddah → a wider Red Sea war raises the risk to Suez Canal traffic and Egypt's shipping costs.
The AI sell-off returns: Seoul's Kospi falls 6.16% and Taiwan 4.94% on Wednesday after the Nasdaq drops 1.5% → doubts over AI returns and new US tariff threats weigh on global risk appetite.
The EGX30 edges up 0.34% to 50,885.33 as Sidpec jumps 5.4% → the index is still 10.2% below its 6 September peak.
Retail investors cover only 0.19x of Misr Life's public tranche on day one → the soft start tests demand for the state's biggest listing of the year.
The EGX30 rebounds 1.44% to 50,711.96 on Monday and small caps jump 3.41%, recovering part of Sunday's sell-off → every stock in the 21-stock table except Emaar Misr rises as global markets steady.

Misr Life Insurance opens its IPO book at EGP 12.00 to 13.60 a share, valuing it at EGP 60 to 68 bn → the whole range sits below the EGP 13.82 fair value set by its adviser; trading is due around 3 December.

Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang and the Nasdaq jumps 6.5%, its best day since April 2025; Taiwan rises about 9% on Tuesday → the AI trade revives after last week's rout, lifting risk appetite worldwide.
Brent falls 3.46% to $89.37, its lowest close since 31 August, as Libya restarts the Sharara pipeline → cheaper oil eases Egypt's fuel import bill.

The EGX30 drops 2.85% to 49,989.79 on Sunday and small caps fall 5.55%, as local investors sell after Wall Street's correction → foreigners are the only net buyers; turnover stays 40.4% below its 90-day average.
Three LNG cargoes bound for Egypt divert to Europe, and fertiliser makers pay 50% more for gas at $12.75/mmBtu → Europe outbids Cairo for scarce cargoes, raising costs for energy-hungry industry.
US stock futures jump 2.2% on Monday after the S&P 500 fell 3.7% on Friday into a correction → a rebound abroad could steady the EGX after Sunday's sell-off.
Tankers are set ablaze in the Strait of Hormuz and the Houthis claim an attack on a Saudi refinery → Gulf attacks keep oil's risk premium alive; Brent holds near $92.7.
Iran strikes US air-defence sites in Bahrain and tankers are hit near Hormuz on Saturday → the Gulf war widens, keeping oil, shipping and insurance risk high for Egypt.
Goldman Sachs sees the CBE holding at 20% until late Q1 2027, then cutting 700 bp by 2028 → it calls the pound more than 30% undervalued and sees no external financing gap through FY2029/30.
Misr Life Insurance, which earned EGP 5.8 bn in 2025, targets a 70% payout ahead of its EGX debut in early December → a large, high-dividend state listing deepens the market.
Orascom Construction breaks ground on Jordan's $6.7 bn Aqaba-Amman water project → the project adds to its backlog before its merger shares list on 24 November.
Wall Street enters a correction: the Nasdaq falls 5.3% and the S&P 500 3.5% on Friday as the AI sell-off deepens → a global risk-off mood can weigh on emerging markets, including the EGX on Sunday.
Gold posts its worst week in eight months, down 8.9%, and 21K gold in Egypt drops 3.04% to EGP 5,575 → markets bet on a December Fed hike, and margin calls force sales.

Saudi-led coalition intercepts three Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh as Gulf war-risk costs climb → tanker insurance from the Middle East to Asia reaches $12.29 a barrel, keeping Red Sea and Suez risk high.
Arab Energy Fund launches a $70 mn tender offer for 21.3% of Maridive at $0.70 a share → a Gulf-backed buyer puts a price on an EGX-listed oil services firm.

stories.h: Suez Canal revenue doubles in November as shipping lines return
stories.what: Suez Canal Authority chairman Ossama Rabiee says revenue since the start of November reaches $593 mn, up 101.2% from $295 mn in the same period last year. Transits rise 34.8% to 1,194 ships, and net tonnage climbs to 72 mn tons from 37 mn tons.
stories.why: Several major shipping lines return to the canal, the SCA says.
stories.aff: Egypt's dollar income, the current account and the pound.
stories.eg: A stronger canal adds steady foreign currency despite the Red Sea risk.
stories.egx: Bullish for banks and Suez-linked services.

key.l: new Orascom Construction shares issued for OCI

stories.h: Orascom closes its OCI deal but its new shares miss the listing date; IFC lends Edita $25 mn
stories.what: Orascom Construction closes its OCI acquisition on 25 November, issuing 97.2 mn new shares and lifting its share count to 207.4 mn; OCI holds about 47%. The new shares are not yet admitted to the EGX or ADX after missing the 24 November target. The record date is 30 November, and OCI holders should receive Orascom shares around 8 December. Separately, the IFC lends Edita $25 mn to more than double its capacity in Iraq.
stories.why: Orascom combines with OCI's infrastructure investments.
stories.aff: Orascom Construction's share supply and Edita's regional growth.
stories.eg: A larger Orascom and new foreign funding for an Egyptian food maker.
stories.egx: Neutral for Orascom until the shares list; bullish for Edita.

stories.h: US inflation stays hot and growth beats forecasts, cementing a December Fed hike
stories.src: Reuters via Investing.com; Investing.com; Al Jazeera
stories.what: US core PCE inflation rises to 3.3% in October, its highest since November 2023, and headline PCE to 3.8%. Third-quarter GDP growth is revised up to 4.3%. Markets price a 98% chance of a December Fed hike. The US also announces new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including 20% on China. On Wall Street the Nasdaq falls 0.62% to 23,585.80 and the S&P 500 0.25%, while the Dow rises 0.33%. South Korea's central bank raises its rate to 3.25%.
stories.why: Strong demand, AI spending and tariffs keep US inflation high.
stories.aff: US rates, the dollar and emerging-market flows.
stories.eg: A higher US rate path makes Egyptian bills less attractive to foreigners.

stories.h: EGX30 slips 0.68% as local investors sell
stories.what: The EGX30 falls 0.68% to 50,538.66 on Wednesday, the EGX70 1.32% and the EGX100 1.23%; market cap is EGP 3.97 tn. Turnover is EGP 6.2 bn, 43.3% below the 90-day average. TMG Holding (+1.1%) and MOPCO (+0.6%) gain, while Raya Holding (-4.2%), AMOC (-2.9%) and Orascom Construction (-2.8%) fall. The CBE quotes the dollar at 54.63 buy and 54.76 sell on Thursday.
stories.why: Local investors are the only net sellers, EnterpriseAM reports.
stories.aff: Blue chips, small caps and the pound.
stories.eg: Caution ahead of the Misr Life listing and the Fed's December meeting.
stories.names: TMG Holding (up); Raya Holding, AMOC, Orascom Construction (down).

stories.h: Houthis hit Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery; more ships hit mines near Hormuz
stories.what: The Houthis strike Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery, and at least two ships hit Iranian mines in the Strait of Hormuz. The coalition intercepts two Houthi missiles over Riyadh, an explosion hits Sanaa, and a tanker reports a blast about 50 nautical miles west of Dubai. Brent rises to $94.71 on Thursday morning. OPEC+ ministers meet on 29 November.
stories.why: The Saudi-Houthi war and the war on Iran target Gulf energy sites and shipping.
stories.aff: Oil prices, Gulf shipping and insurance.
stories.eg: Higher oil prices raise Egypt's fuel import bill.

stories.h: Cabinet widens the 15% industrial loan scheme; Arcius plans $1 bn gas spend
stories.what: The cabinet splits the EGP 30 bn industrial financing initiative into EGP 15 bn for machinery and EGP 15 bn for working capital, with loans at 15%, and raises the limit for strategic projects to EGP 200 mn. Separately, Arcius Energy, owned by XRG and BP, plans about $1 bn of investment in Egypt in 2027 and expects its Harmattan gas field to start at 200 mn cubic feet a day before mid-2028. GM Egypt starts Chevrolet Groove production with 45% local content.
stories.why: The government wants to boost local production and gas output.
stories.aff: Manufacturers, gas supply and the trade balance.
stories.eg: Cheaper credit for factories and more domestic gas later.
